root_cause.text: In ceph_mdsc_build_path(), memory allocated by __getname() for the path buffer was not freed on error paths where the function returns ERR_PTR without passing ownership to the caller, causing memory leaks.

agent_logs.root_cause_candidate: In ceph_mdsc_build_path(), memory allocated by __getname() for the path buffer was not freed on error paths where the function returns ERR_PTR without passing ownership to the caller, causing memory leaks.

intent_record.intent_summary: Fix memory leak by freeing the path buffer before returning an error in ceph_mdsc_build_path.
intent_record.what: Added `__putname(path);` before returning ERR_PTR(ret) in the error handling block of ceph_mdsc_build_path.
intent_record.how: The change ensures that the dynamically allocated path buffer is freed when an error occurs, preventing a memory leak.

intent_record.intent_summary: Add missing `__putname(path)` in error path to prevent memory leak.
intent_record.what: Added a call to `__putname(path)` in the error handling block when `len < 0` before returning `ERR_PTR(len)`.
intent_record.how: Prevents a memory leak by freeing the previously allocated `path` buffer when an error occurs, ensuring proper cleanup.

intent_record.intent_summary: Fix memory leak by freeing the path buffer when the constructed path exceeds PATH_MAX.
intent_record.what: Added a call to __putname(path) before returning ERR_PTR(-ENAMETOOLONG) in ceph_mdsc_build_path when the path exceeds the maximum allowed length.
intent_record.how: This ensures that the memory allocated for the path buffer is freed on the error path, preventing a memory leak that would otherwise occur when the path is too long.

grouping_result.intent: Fix memory leak by freeing the path buffer when the constructed path exceeds PATH_MAX.

consistency_review.core_intent: Fix memory leaks by freeing the path buffer in error paths in ceph_mdsc_build_path.

relevance_review.reason: The group's core intent and all hunks focus on freeing the path buffer in error paths of ceph_mdsc_build_path, directly addressing the memory leak described in the root cause.

candidates.rationale: This return statement does not free the path buffer allocated by __getname(), causing a memory leak when ret < 0.
Similarly, when len < 0, the path buffer is not freed before returning an error.
When the path exceeds PATH_MAX, the function returns an error without freeing the path buffer.

vuln_statements.explanation: On error path where ret < 0, the function returns ERR_PTR(ret) without freeing the path buffer allocated by __getname(), causing a memory leak.
When len < 0, the function returns ERR_PTR(len) without freeing the path buffer, leading to a memory leak.
When the constructed path exceeds PATH_MAX, the function returns ERR_PTR(-ENAMETOOLONG) without freeing the path buffer, causing a memory leak.

bic_trace_step.reason: The commit introduces new error return paths in ceph_mdsc_build_path (e.g., when __fscrypt_prepare_readdir fails, returning ERR_PTR(ret); and when ceph_encode_encrypted_fname fails, returning ERR_PTR(len)). In neither case is the path buffer (allocated via __getname) freed before returning. This directly matches the described root cause of memory leaks on error paths. No fix (i.e., freeing the buffer) is present in these new paths.

bic_trace_step.reason: In this commit, ceph_mdsc_build_path() allocates path buffer with kmalloc() (line 'path = kmalloc(len+1, GFP_NOFS);'), not __getname(). The only error path after allocation is when pos != 0, where kfree(path) is called before retrying (lines 'kfree(path); goto retry;'). bic_trace_step.commit_msg:
ceph: give up on paths longer than PATH_MAX

If the full path to be built by ceph_mdsc_build_path() happens to be
longer
bic_trace_step.code_snippet:
commit 550f7ca98ee028a606aa75705a7e77b1bd11720f
Author: Max Kellermann <max.kellermann@ionos.com>
Date:   Mon Nov 18 23:28:28 2024 +0100

    ceph: give up on paths longer than PATH_MAX
    
    If the full path to be built by ceph_mdsc_build_path() happens to be
    longer than PATH_MAX, then this function will enter an endless (retry)
    loop, effectively blocking the whole task.  Most of the machine
    becomes unusable, making this a very simple and effective DoS
    vulnerability.
bic_trace_step.reason: The function body shows two direct ERR_PTR returns at lines 2762 and 2771 that do not free the path buffer allocated by __getname(). The vulnerability root cause is that memory is not freed on these error paths, and the fix (adding __putname(path) before returning) is absent.
